b1: Every enterprise has more ideas than it can build.
b2: Put AI inside ideation, and every idea can become a software system.
b3: AI writes code in minutes, but an enterprise needs a system that is ready for production.
b4: Akka is an AI platform that turns any idea into a system that is ready for production, and keeps it trustworthy once it runs.
b5: Only Akka combines the path from an idea to a specification, the pipeline that builds and checks the system, and the runtime the system is built for.
b6: Because the runtime is known before any code is generated, AI writes less, and reviewers review less.
b7: The design space is fixed before code is generated.
b8: AI generates only from Akka components, and each system is still its own design.
b9: The hardest requirements are satisfied by the runtime: identity, durability, replication, failover, scaling, sharding, circuit breakers, caching, and backpressure.
b10: An enterprise's requirements are written as exit conditions.
b11: A machine checks each condition wherever it can, and the human attestations are recorded alongside.
b12: The enterprise tightens the conditions where it needs to.
b13: A conformance receipt states that the system is ready to ship.
b14: The laptop runtime and the production runtime are the same, so the system goes to production as it was built.
b15: The system stays trustworthy after the build.
b16: The security, identity, controls, and interaction model that applied at build time also apply in production.
b17: Every change to a specification is documented with a machine-generated receipt of what was verified, what remains open, and any waivers.
b18: The receipts are an evidence trail that a requirement a user asked for was implemented and verified.
b19: Akka captures production traces, evaluations, and cost, and they feed the next improvement to the specification.
b20: Akka systems run wherever you need them: in our cloud, in your datacenter, or in a sovereign cloud.
b21: Every idea goes through the same stations: discovery, specify, plan, build, conform, and ship.
b22: Every station passes versioned records to the next.
b23: Where a decision is ambiguous, a human is asked to provide the clarifications needed to eliminate the ambiguity, and the answers are recorded with the station's records.
b24: The organization sees its portfolio of ideas, and where each idea stands.
b25: Akka can rebuild and replatform an existing system to functional and behavioral parity with the original system.
b26: Akka uses the existing system as a testbed and answer key.
b27: Feedback, spend, and human judgement decide which idea goes next.

b29: Legacy liability reduction is the saving from the technical debt, unsupported software, mainframes, and licenses you retire.
